items.appliesWhen: You set --banner-ic-mt anywhere. It is a global geometry token, not a --ds-* component hook, so an app that only overrides --ds-banner-* is unaffected.
items.pitfall: Deleting the override is the whole fix, but only because the icon no longer needs nudging: it is now centred on the message block rather than aligned to the first line. If you had raised the value to line the icon up with a taller first line, that adjustment is now working against the new rule and will push the icon off centre.
items.verify: A ds-banner with two or more lines of body text shows its icon vertically centred on the text block, and no rule in your app references --banner-ic-mt.
items.restore: align-self: flex-start on the banner's .icon reproduces the old first-line alignment, if you need it while migrating.
items.note: The token was one border-width of optical bump, and it existed only to serve the first-line alignment rule. With the icon centred on the block there is nothing left for it to correct, and it was read from exactly one declaration.
items.action: Delete any --banner-ic-mt declaration. There is no replacement token.

informational: The banner and toast icon now centres on the message block instead of aligning to the first line of text. Nothing to change: it is a visual default, applied by the components themselves. One-line messages look identical either way, which covers most toasts; the difference grows with the text, and was 12px at two lines and 21px at three. If you deliberately want the old alignment, set `align-self: flex-start` on the icon.
